analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. In docs/provider/cli-reference.md, the only changed head lines are 1751-1753, which add three DARKBLOOM_TTFT_* rows to the daemon passthrough table. The table is the LaunchAgent plist passthrough list, so the new variables are read by GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift and EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift. In docs/provider/direct-mode.md (hunk at lines 44-50), the standalone-server preload text now describes retained paged KV segments being released and the MLX buffer cache dropped before the least recently used idle slot is evicted.

Threat relevance: T-041 and T-028 (residual KV/GPU memory, prefix cache, TTFT oracle), TB-007 (inference engine) and TB-003 (operator vs process). These are doc changes only, with no changed code, so no control is demonstrably weakened.

Unverified contract: the source behind the TTFT_* tuning flags (idle cache sweep, segment retention, host zeros) is not supplied. If DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION widens retention of KV segments or changes zeroing behavior, T-028 residual-data and T-041 timing-oracle assumptions could be affected, and those env passthroughs could be set by the operator (ADV-001 already has local control). The TTL, HMAC and salt posture of the SSD tier is unchanged and these env vars do not appear to touch it. A later code review should confirm that the retention and host-zeros flags do not extend retention of plaintext KV across tenants, and that the standalone/direct-mode eviction path (StandaloneServer.ensureMemoryHeadroomForLoad) clears released segments. Nothing else in the three cli-reference units changed. No findings are raised on this evidence alone.
